questions.question: You create a list with new ArrayList<>() and add one item. What is the capacity of the internal array now?
questions.explanation: The no-argument constructor starts with an empty array and allocates the default capacity of 10 on the first add.

questions.question: Which formula does ArrayList use to find its new capacity when the array is full?
questions.explanation: old >> 1 is half of old, so the array grows to about 1.5 times its size: 10, 15, 22, 33 and so on.

questions.question: What does this print? List<Integer> a = new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(4, 1, 7)); a.remove(1); System.out.println(a);
questions.explanation: remove(1) with an int argument removes the item at index 1, which is the value 1 here by chance, leaving [4, 7].

questions.question: What does this print? List<String> s = new ArrayList<>(); s.add("A"); s.add("B"); s.add(0, "X"); System.out.println(s);
questions.explanation: add(0, X) inserts at the front and shifts A and B one place to the right. Nothing is replaced.

questions.question: for (String o : orders) { if (o.isEmpty()) orders.remove(o); } Why can this loop fail?
options: isEmpty() is not a String method
Removing through the list inside a for-each loop can throw ConcurrentModificationException
for-each does not work on ArrayList
remove() needs an index, not an object
questions.explanation: The hidden iterator detects the change in the list. Use orders.removeIf(String::isEmpty) or an explicit Iterator.

questions.question: List<String> cakes = Arrays.asList("Bun", "Puff"); cakes.add("Tart"); What happens?
options: Tart is added at the end
questions.explanation: Arrays.asList returns a fixed-size list backed by an array. Wrap it in new ArrayList<>(...) to make it growable.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of get(i) on an ArrayList with n items?
questions.explanation: The item sits at a known slot in the internal array, so it is read directly without walking the list.

questions.question: What does this print? List<String> t = new ArrayList<>(50); System.out.println(t.size());
questions.explanation: 50 is the starting capacity of the hidden array. size() counts stored items, and none were added.

questions.question: Which statement about ArrayList is true?
options: It keeps insertion order and allows duplicates and null
questions.explanation: ArrayList is an ordered, index-based list. It never sorts on its own, accepts repeats and null, and is not synchronized.

questions.question: What does this print? List<String> l = new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList("a", "b", "a")); System.out.println(l.indexOf("a") + " " + l.lastIndexOf("a"));
questions.explanation: indexOf returns the first match at index 0, and lastIndexOf returns the last match at index 2.
